why:
Run the roster in time order. Each grower sees only the running total recorded before their own single consultation (e2, e5), and the board shows nothing else (e2).
  Mon 13 Apr 10:00 -- Vetch: commits 6 unconditionally (e7). Total 6.
  Mon 13 Apr 14:00 -- Ackley: board shows 6; her threshold is 5; 6 >= 5, so she commits 4 (e8). Total 10.
  Tue 14 Apr 08:30 -- Nakadai: board shows 10; his threshold is 12; 10 < 12, so he commits nothing (e9). He consults the board exactly once and does not return (e5), so his 3 pallets never enter the total at any later point.
  Tue 14 Apr 11:00 -- Brenner: board shows 10; threshold 9; 10 >= 9, so he commits 8 (e10). Total 18.
  Tue 14 Apr 16:00 -- Quinto: board shows 18; threshold 15; 18 >= 15, so she commits 5 (e11). Total 23.
  Wed 15 Apr 09:00 -- Renfrew: board shows 23; threshold 25; 23 < 25, so he commits nothing (e12). He too consults once only and does not return.
  Wed 15 Apr 15:00 -- Aldous: board shows 23; threshold 20; 23 >= 20, so she commits 2 (e13). Total 25.
  No further slot falls before the close. The board closes at 5:00 PM Thursday 16 April showing 25 pallets (e1).
  Ferrar's rostered slot is 5:30 PM Thursday 16 April (e14) -- half an hour AFTER the close. No commitment can be recorded then and the depot manager has no discretion to accept one (e3), so her 9 pallets never enter the total either.
Commitments cannot be withdrawn (e4) and no grower learns anything off the board (e6), so 6 + 4 + 8 + 5 + 2 = 25.
ANSWER: 25 pallets.
NAIVE WRONG ANSWER. A system that solves for a fixed point -- asking which growers' thresholds are satisfied by the FINAL total rather than by the total visible at each grower's own slot -- concludes that Nakadai qualifies (12 <= 25) and that Renfrew qualifies (25 <= 25), and reports 6 + 4 + 3 + 8 + 5 + 7 + 2 = 35. If it also admits Ferrar (24 <= 35) it reports 44. Both are wrong. The order of consultation is what decides each grower: Nakadai and Renfrew each looked exactly once and each looked too early, and Ferrar looked after the board had shut. The near-miss at Renfrew is the sharp edge of the case -- the board does reach exactly 25, his threshold, later that same afternoon, but only after his single consultation had already passed.
